approachQuestion.prompt:
Choose exactly k distinct indices from a read-only array of n unsigned W-bit values. Return the largest possible bitwise AND of the k chosen values. Only the maximum word is required, not the chosen indices.

Constraints: 1 <= W <= 64; 1 <= k <= n <= 200000.
Example: W=4, values=[8,7,6], k=2 -> 6, by choosing 7 and 6. Edge case: k=n -> the AND of the full array.

Choose the best approach under these constraints.
constraints: W is a width parameter. A W-bit mask operation and unsigned comparison cost constant time. Index/count words can hold n. Inputs must not be reordered or copied implicitly.
Inputs are read-only. Include all temporary storage and any call stack; exclude the supplied input and the returned output. No input copy is implicit.

options.text: Start answer=0. Try each bit from high to low: candidate=answer with that bit set. Scan the entire array and count values v for which (v AND candidate)=candidate. Keep candidate exactly when the count is at least k.
options.feedback: A candidate is achievable exactly when at least k values contain all its bits. Keeping feasible high bits maximizes the unsigned result without losing feasibility.

options.text: Copy all values to a candidate list. For each high-to-low bit, if at least k current candidates have that bit, keep the bit and filter the list to those candidates; otherwise leave the list unchanged.
options.feedback: This preserves the same feasible candidate invariant and is correct, but stores a list that can be replaced by rescanning the original array for the full growing mask.

options.text: Set every result bit that appears in at least k input values, treating bits independently.
options.feedback: Different bits may be supported by different groups. For [6,5,3], k=2, it returns 7, although the best pair AND is 4.

options.text: Select the k numerically largest values and AND them.
options.feedback: For [8,7,6] and k=2, this returns 0 from 8 AND 7, while 7 AND 6 is 6.

feedback.reason: A proposed answer mask is feasible exactly when at least k inputs contain every one of its bits.
details: Grow a feasible mask from the most significant bit downward. To test a proposed added bit, scan all inputs for values containing every bit of that complete mask. Accept the bit only when at least k values qualify. Keep only the mask and counters, since no witness subset is requested.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For test-growing-mask, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let n be the number of values and W the bit width. The analyzed method scans the entire array for every trial bit.
constraints: W is a width parameter. A W-bit mask operation and unsigned comparison cost constant time. Index/count words can hold n. Inputs must not be reordered or copied implicitly.
Inputs are read-only. Include all temporary storage and any call stack; exclude the supplied input and the returned output. No input copy is implicit.

feedback.reason: Perform one full n-value feasibility scan for each of W trial bits.
details: There are W trial bits and each has a full n-element scan. A candidate mask, answer, counters and indices use constant auxiliary words. There is no witness list, copy or recursion.
W is a width parameter. A W-bit mask operation and unsigned comparison cost constant time. Index/count words can hold n. Inputs must not be reordered or copied implicitly.
“O(nW) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: This corresponds to retaining a candidate-list copy, absent from the analyzed method.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: There are W trial masks; W is not fixed here.
“O(n²W) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The method counts support for one mask at a time, not every value pair.
